chunks: (The Pharaoh) said: "Did we not bring you up as a child among us, and you lived with us for a number of years of your life?"

key_terms.وَلِيدًا: a child raised in a house

ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh say to Prophet Musa regarding his upbringing in Egypt?
ai.summary: Pharaoh employs this rhetorical question to highlight the irony of Musa’s prophetic mission, contrasting his privileged upbringing as a 'walid' (child/young man) in the royal household with his current rejection of Egyptian authority. In Shia exegesis, this underscores the theme of divine selection transcending social status, as Musa, though raised in the palace, remained distinct in faith and purpose. The verse also serves as a precursor to Musa’s eventual departure, marking the end of his formative years in Egypt.
